description: Implement mo attach CLI command for real-time agent monitoring via SSE

tasks.title: Implement SSE client parser
tasks.description: Create a simple SSE client using Node.js built-in http module. It should: (1) Connect to a URL via http.get, (2) Parse SSE format (event: and data: lines), (3) Emit parsed events via callback, (4) Handle connection errors and close. This is a utility function, not a class.
acceptanceCriteria: Function connectSSE(url, { onEvent, onError, onClose }) implemented
Correctly parses event: and data: lines
Handles multi-line data (concatenates with newlines)
Calls onClose when connection ends
Calls onError on connection failure
No new npm dependencies
tasks.notes: SSE format: lines starting with 'event:' set event type, lines starting with 'data:' set data, empty line dispatches. Keep it simple.

tasks.title: Implement event formatter
tasks.description: Create a formatter function that takes an SSE event (type + parsed JSON data) and returns a formatted string with timestamp, symbol, event description, and issue info. Use chalk for coloring. Supported event types: agent_started, agent_completed, agent_paused, agent_error, stage_changed, comment_added, approval_requested.
acceptanceCriteria: Each event type has a distinct color and symbol
Format: [HH:MM:SS] SYMBOL event description  issue #N ...
agent_started: green >>, agent_completed: green ok, agent_paused: yellow ||, agent_error: red !!, stage_changed: cyan ->, comment_added: white ##, approval_requested: yellow ??
Timestamp uses local time
Handles unknown event types gracefully (prints raw data)
tasks.notes: Don't use emoji. Use ASCII symbols: >>, ->, ##, ||, ok, !!, ??.

tasks.title: Implement mo attach command
tasks.description: Create cli/commands/attach.ts with setupAttachCommand(program). Command options: --project <name> (optional, defaults to current project), --follow (auto-reconnect on disconnect with 2s delay). The command should: call requireServer(), resolve project name to ID via API if --project specified, build SSE URL with projectId filter, connect and print events, handle SIGINT/SIGTERM for graceful detach.
acceptanceCriteria: mo attach command registered in Commander program
mo attach --project myapp filters by project (resolve name to ID via /api/projects)
mo attach --follow reconnects on disconnect with 2s delay
Ctrl+C prints 'Detached.' and exits cleanly
SIGTERM handled same as SIGINT
Server not running shows error: 'Error: Server is not running' and 'Start the server with: mo server start'
tasks.notes: Follow the pattern of existing command files (issue.ts, project.ts). Register in cli/index.ts. Use existing requireServer() from cli/index.ts.

tasks.title: Add unit tests for SSE client and formatter
tasks.description: Add automated tests for SSE client parser and event formatter functions. Mock http module for SSE tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests for connectSSE: parsing events, handling multi-line data, error handling
Tests for formatEvent: all 7 event types, unknown events, timestamp formatting
All tests pass with npm test
tasks.notes: Mock http.get for unit testing. Create test fixtures for SSE event streams.

tasks.title: Backend fix: add agent_paused to SSE subscriptions
tasks.description: Add 'agent_paused' to ALL_EVENT_TYPES array in /api/events.ts to enable pause events to be sent via SSE.
acceptanceCriteria: agent_paused added to ALL_EVENT_TYPES array
When agent pauses, || agent paused message appears in mo attach output
tasks.notes: This is a necessary backend fix. Without it, agent_paused events won't reach the client.

tasks.title: Build and manual integration test
tasks.description: Build, typecheck, and manual test: start server, run mo attach in another terminal, start an issue, verify events appear in attach output. Test reconnect with --follow by restarting server.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run build succeeds
Typecheck passes
mo attach connects and displays events
Ctrl+C exits cleanly
mo attach --follow reconnects after server restart
tasks.notes: Manual test checklist: 1) Start server, 2) Run mo attach, 3) Create and start issue, 4) Verify events flow, 5) Stop server (verify --follow reconnects), 6) Restart server (verify events continue), 7) Ctrl+C to detach.
